content.comment_body: Hello, I have 9 [product_name] modules networked together. When attempting to establish more Network Input connections, I receive the error message: "The maximum number of connections has been reached." Currently, I've created a total of 19 Network Inputs to the first [product_name] module. Is this the maximum number of Network Inputs one module can support? I thought the limit was 64 network inputs. Is there a possible solution for this? All modules are set as master.

"The maximum number of connections has been reached" doesn't necessarily mean you have exceeded the number of network inputs. The message indicates that if you try to create any additional connection, you have hit the overall connection limit. Could you share the [project_file] or all related configuration files?
To resolve this, you may consider switching from [product_name] to a different controller such as [version_no], which supports a greater number of connections.
The TP700 is a Comfort Panel. This type of panel can handle up to 8 connections.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum participants have encountered a restriction on the number of network connections when connecting multiple [product_name] modules. The primary concern stems from a system message about exceeding the connection limit, which brings confusion regarding the distinction between network input limits and total connection limits. There is also uncertainty over the restrictions of both the [product_name] module and the associated HMI panel, resulting in a lack of clear knowledge about the system's capacities.
analysis.user_expectations: The user anticipates being able to use up to 64 network input connections per [product_name] module and seeks clear guidance on connection restrictions and possible methods to increase the allowable number of connections.
